Stop 1

We made the team

Zentral Hack → SDG 11

From one idea to five people

It started with Abbas alone: waste-bin sensors, picked from the Swiss SDG 11 report. Everyone sees overflowing bins, and a prototype is quick to build.

Then he built the team around it: design, data, development and backend. Five people, two days.

2
Stop 2

What was the problem?

Bins are emptied on a fixed schedule: half-empty ones get emptied, full ones overflow.

~1,350public bins in Basel
~21,800 hwork per year to empty them
  • Fixed routes. Trucks stop at every bin, full or empty.
  • Overflowing bins. Litter, smell and complaints between pickups.
  • Wasted time and fuel. Crews empty bins that are half full.
  • No data. The city can't see which bins fill fast, or where.
  • Sensors failed before. Bern stopped two pilots because of false readings.

Example values for Basel

3
Stop 3

How did we solve it?

Sensors report the fill level. We filter wrong readings and send the truck only where it is needed.

Sensors1,000+ simulated sensors. Buffer 1 h, upload one batch per hour.
MQTT 5 · TLS
BrokerEclipse Mosquitto collects every message.
subscribe
ProcessingNode-RED now, .NET later. Validate, decode, drop duplicates.invalid → dead-letter topic
SQL
DatabasePostgreSQL + TimescaleDB: time series and bin data.
read
Smart layerFault check, fill-level forecast, truck route.
show
DashboardWeb dashboard and the crew map with the route.
Simulated week, 40 Basel bins: 48 % fewer unnecessary emptyings.
